project.title: Nanostructures regulate cell adhesion behavior through mechanotransduction-mediated signaling pathways
project.projectDescription: Nanotopography has a significant regulatory effect on cell adhesion behavior. We fabricated titanium alloy surfaces with titanium dioxide nanotubes using electrochemical anodization, which exhibited increased surface roughness and superhydrophilicity. Using single-cell force spectroscopy, we observed that the nanotubular structure altered the mechanical forces experienced at the cell-surface interface. Proteomic analysis revealed that Nesprin-1 protein transmits these signals to the intracellular core signaling system, leading to the upregulation and activation of GSK3β, STAT3, and related pathways. These events regulate cytoskeletal remodeling and adhesion complex assembly, thereby promoting cell adhesion.
project.sampleProcessingProtocol: Sterilized samples (Φ30 × 1 mm) were placed in 6-well plates, inoculated with 100 µL of S. aureus suspension (1 × 10⁵ CFU/mL), and submerged with 2 mL of antibiotic-free culture medium. Following 8 h of static incubation, adhered bacteria were collected by scraping, pelleted by centrifugation (15,000 rpm, 5 min), washed thrice with cold PBS, and resuspended in 500 µL cold PBS. Bacterial lysis was achieved via ultrasonication. Lysates were centrifuged (15,000 rpm, 10 min, 4 °C), and the supernatant was collected. Protein concentration was quantified using a BCA assay, and all samples were normalized to an equal concentration. Proteins were separated by SDS-PAGE using a 5% stacking and a 10% resolving gel. After electrophoresis, gels were stained with Coomassie Brilliant Blue, and protein bands were excised and diced. Gel pieces were destained, dehydrated with acetonitrile, reduced with 10 mM DTT (56 °C, 30 min), and alkylated with 55 mM iodoacetamide (room temperature, dark, 20 min). In-gel digestion was performed overnight at 37 °C using trypsin (1.2 ng/µL) in 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate. Peptides were extracted with 50% acetonitrile containing 5% formic acid, dried, and stored at -80 °C. LC-MS/MS analysis was performed using an EASY-nLC 1200 system coupled to an LTQ Orbitrap Velos mass spectrometer. Peptides were separated on a C18 analytical column with a gradient from 8% to 40% acetonitrile over 45 min and ionized via nano-electrospray. MS spectra (m/z 400-1200) were acquired in the Orbitrap at 60,000 resolution, and the top 10 precursors were selected for CID MS/MS in the ion trap.
project.dataProcessingProtocol: The acquired .raw files were processed using MaxQuant software (version not specified in analysis) against the UniProt database. Database search parameters allowed up to three missed cleavages, a mass tolerance of 20 ppm for precursors and 0.8 Da for fragments, carbamidomethylation of cysteine as a fixed modification, and methionine oxidation as a variable modification. The false discovery rate (FDR) was controlled at <1%. Relative protein quantification was based on spectral counting, using the total number of identified spectra per protein as an index of abundance. Differentially expressed proteins (DEPs) were defined with thresholds of p < 0.05 and |log₂ fold change| > 1. For bioinformatic analysis, DEPs were subjected to Gene Ontology (GO) functional annotation (Cellular Component, Molecular Function, Biological Process), KEGG pathway enrichment analysis, and analysis using the DAVID database to identify involved biological processes and signaling pathways.
